references.text: Isaac loved Rebekah – another example of love leading to marriage in the patriarchal family.
Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they seemed to him like only a few days because he loved her – the direct fulfillment of his offer.
Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah, confirming the deep love that motivated his service.
Jacob asks Laban to let him take his wives and children after serving him, showing his commitment to Rachel.
Jacob summarizes his twenty years with Laban: fourteen years for his two daughters and six years for the flocks – his long service testifies to his love for Rachel.
Hosea refers to Jacob fleeing to Aram and serving for a woman, a direct prophetic reference to his service for Rachel.
The fulfillment of the promise in 29:18 where Laban finally gives Rachel to Jacob after the completed period of service.
Direct continuation of dialogue where Laban responds to Jacob's offer of seven years of work.
